title: FIFO Queues, Ordering & Exactly-Once Processing
summary: When order and deduplication matter: SQS FIFO, SNS FIFO, message groups and idempotency.
tldr: **SQS FIFO** keeps strict order *within a message group* and drops duplicates sent within the 5-minute deduplication interval. **Standard** queues are at-least-once with best-effort order but nearly unlimited throughput.
Set the **message group ID** to the entity that needs ordering (account, trader, instrument). Different groups are processed in parallel; one group for everything kills throughput.
Need ordered **fan-out** to several services? Publish to an **SNS FIFO** topic and subscribe one SQS FIFO queue per service.
Can't change a standard queue, or duplicates come from the consumer side? Make the consumer **idempotent** (DynamoDB conditional write on a request ID).

keyFacts.text: The FIFO **deduplication interval**. A message with the same deduplication ID (or same body, with content-based deduplication) is accepted but not delivered again.
Default FIFO limit per API action (send, receive, delete) without batching; batches of 10 give up to **3,000 messages per second**.
**High throughput mode** sets deduplication scope and the throughput limit to the **message group**, raising limits far above 300/s. Use many distinct group IDs.
FIFO queue and topic names must end in `.fifo`. A standard queue can't be converted to FIFO; create a new queue and move the app.
FIFO queues support a delay on the whole queue but **not per-message timers**; per-message delays are a standard-queue feature.

keywords.answer: SQS FIFO with message group ID = account ID

keywords.answer: SQS FIFO with MessageGroupId per trader

traps: A single message group ID for all messages forces one-at-a-time processing and caps throughput.
Content-based deduplication exists only on **FIFO** queues and topics, not on standard queues.
A longer visibility timeout reduces redelivery but does **not** guarantee exactly-once processing.
An SNS **standard** topic in front of SQS FIFO queues loses the ordering guarantee; the topic must be FIFO too.
EventBridge rules don't guarantee delivery order, so routing through an event bus is a weak answer for strict per-entity ordering.
Several services polling **one** queue compete for messages; each message goes to only one of them.
Spreading messages randomly across several FIFO queues breaks per-entity ordering; enable high throughput mode instead.
Reserved concurrency of 1 slows everything down and still doesn't remove duplicates.
